findings.what: `prepare_image` always computes the step-7 cells with the `pixel` geometry. It takes no `renderer` argument, but `render(..., renderer=X)` resolves its palette on X's geometry.
findings.why: Apps use the pair `resolve_palette(prepare_image(...))` → `render_with_palette(..., renderer=X)`. Once a non-square renderer exists (L3+), that path will resolve the palette on different cells than `render()` does. The difference is invisible today because only `pixel` is registered.
findings.fix: Add a keyword-only argument `renderer: str = DEFAULT_RENDERER` to `prepare_image` and pass it to `_cell_geometry`, matching `render` and `render_with_palette`.

findings.what: `_cell_geometry` fixes `cell_w = pixel_size` and rounds `cell_h = round(size/aspect)` with Python's round-half-to-even. When aspect > 1 and the pixel size is small, the cell aspect is lost: aspect 2.0 at `pixel_size` 1 gives 1×1. `cell_h` is also not clamped to `MAX_PIXEL_SIZE`.
findings.why: Invariant 4 has the pipeline honour `cell_aspect()`. No renderer with aspect > 1 exists yet, so nothing breaks today.
findings.fix: Anchor the larger side on `pixel_size`: if aspect >= 1, set `cell_h = size` and `cell_w = round(size*aspect)`; otherwise keep the current rule. Clamp both sides to [1, MAX_PIXEL_SIZE·k], or document the asymmetry.

findings.what: `_render_frame` duck-types `render_frame` with `getattr` and never checks that the returned frame has shape `(rows*cell_h, cols*cell_w, 3)`. `FloatFrameRenderer` is declared but never used for the check.
findings.why: Invariant 1 is tested only through `render()`. A future renderer whose `render_frame` and `render` disagree on size would be cropped or broadcast silently in the pipeline.
findings.fix: Use `isinstance(renderer, FloatFrameRenderer)` and assert the frame shape against the grid geometry, raising `ValueError` naming the renderer.

findings.what: The Rec.709 linear-luma formula appears twice, in `_make_grid` and in `_coverage_table`.
findings.why: The two copies can drift apart, and coverage and luma must use the same `lum()` from §3.
findings.fix: Extract `_linear_luma(rgb: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray` operating on the last axis and call it from both.

findings.what: Some docstrings are now wrong. `render` still says "eleven normative pipeline steps" when §5 now has 12. `render_with_palette` says "skipping step 5's resolution" when palette resolution is step 8.
findings.why: A docstring that is wrong is a minor finding under the hygiene check (point 9).
findings.fix: Say "the twelve steps of §5" and "skipping step 8 (palette resolution)".

findings.what: `RenderStyle` is frozen but stores the caller's mutable mapping. The JSON check in `__post_init__` can be bypassed by mutating the dict after construction.
findings.why: Invariant 6 is enforced only at construction time.
findings.fix: Store a defensive copy, for example `object.__setattr__(self, 'options', json.loads(encoded))` or a `MappingProxyType` over a copy.

findings.what: `# noqa: F401` duplicates the `__all__` declaration. Registration also happens as an import side effect, so `importlib.reload` raises `ValueError`. `cell.get_renderer('pixel')` raises `KeyError` unless `lattice_core.renderers` has been imported.
findings.why: This is a hygiene issue and a trap for callers that import only `lattice_core.cell`.
findings.fix: Drop the noqa. Have `register_pixel_renderer` skip registration when `pixel` is already registered with the same type. Document that `lattice_core.renderers` must be imported, or import it lazily from `get_renderer`.

regression: none. On the `pixel` path, `_to_cells` delegates to `color.downscale` and `render_frame` uses `apply_palette` plus a per-axis repeat, cropped to the target. The orchestrator's independent check against the HEAD module (25 trials, unaligned float palettes, with and without post-effects) found 0 bytes of difference. `prepare_image` still returns the step-7 image.
renderer_invariants: All six hold for PixelRenderer. Invariant 4 is honoured by `_cell_geometry` for aspect ≤ 1; aspect > 1 at small pixel sizes collapses to square cells (latent, minor). Invariant 6 is enforced only at construction.
tests_that_cannot_fail: test_invariant_renderer_name_is_stable: `len(names) == len(set(names))` — the names come from dict keys, so they are always unique (the `== 'pixel'` assertions can fail)
test_pipeline_derives_grid_geometry_from_cell_aspect: `out_aspect == approx(30/20)` holds for any cell shape that divides 20×30 (the `(1, 2)` assertion can fail)
test_pipeline_preserves_source_aspect_with_square_cells: the `rel=0.1` aspect check holds for any cell geometry (the `(3, 3)` assertion can fail)
test_invariant_style_options_round_trip_json: restates `__post_init__`; the two rejection tests carry the weight
test_protocol_conformance: `runtime_checkable` isinstance only checks that the attributes exist
notes: All five pass-1 findings are resolved. The float32 frame now reaches the post-effects without 8-bit rounding. Parity runs through the public `render_with_palette` and includes a negative control against the rounded path. `cell_aspect` drives the geometry. `RenderStyle` enforces invariant 6. All six accept items are covered. No E8/E9: `lattice_core` imports no application. The main forward risk is that `prepare_image` ignores the renderer; fix it before L3 adds a non-square renderer.
